question: Can persistent homology, supervised parameter recovery, inverse localization, and clustering turn snapshots of simulated magnetic-domain evolution into physically interpretable pattern classes and then motivate a reduced energy-landscape account of continuous versus nucleation-like domain formation?

key_findings.claim: The proposed workflow represents each final grayscale magnetic-domain field by one-dimensional cubical persistent homology and deliberately preserves short-lived generators as possible physical signal.
key_findings.evidence: A superlevel filtration of the magnetic moment is implemented as a sublevel filtration of its negative on a periodic 512 by 512 pixel domain. Persistence diagrams are convolved with Gaussian kernels and sampled on an M by M grid; unlike the standard persistence-image construction, the histogram is not lifetime-weighted because near-diagonal generators are hypothesized to encode intradomain fluctuations. The diagram is manually split into long- and short-life regions according to the observed distribution rather than by one global lifetime cutoff.

key_findings.claim: Ridge regression recovers anisotropy alpha extremely accurately from the persistent-image features, while external-field sweep rate is recovered much less precisely but better than a permuted-label null.
key_findings.evidence: On 96 nondivergent simulations with alpha and log10 sweep rate sampled uniformly, nested cross-validation jointly tunes ridge regularization, Gaussian width, and grid size. The paper reports alpha RMSE about 0.001 and R-squared above 0.99 for the full diagram. Figure 6 shows visibly noisier log-v predictions, and Appendix E establishes only that their RMSE beats a permutation distribution; no numerical effect size, p-value, confidence interval, seed variation, or conventional image-feature baseline is supplied.

key_findings.claim: The inverse analysis associates long-lived generators with whole-domain geometry and short-lived generators with local magnetic-moment fluctuations.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 localizes one representative long-life death cube within each isolated inverse domain and places short-life death cubes around small local peaks. The separate regressions are consistent with short generators carrying most alpha information and long generators retaining sweep-rate information. This is an interpretable correlation inside the simulator, not a causal isolation: the regions are manually drawn and no ablation perturbs the localized structures while holding other image statistics fixed.

key_findings.claim: K-means produces an 11-color partition and a two-dimensional PCA embedding that broadly track alpha and sweep rate, after which the authors manually define six coarser pattern regions I through VI.
key_findings.evidence: K=11 is chosen by an elbow plot on only 96 vectors; the first two principal components explain more than 85 percent of variance and form a roughly circular embedding. Figure 7 overlays cluster colors in parameter space and then draws six dashed parameter regions with examples ranging from labyrinths to sea-island patterns. Hierarchical clustering at K=11 and spectral clustering at K=9 produce only qualitatively similar maps under hand-specified settings, and the mapping from 11 algorithmic clusters to six physical states is not formalized.

key_findings.claim: The apparent unsupervised discovery is not independent of the known simulator controls because the persistence representation used for clustering is first selected by supervised prediction of those same controls.
key_findings.evidence: Section 4.3 explicitly selects sigma and M from the alpha-regression analysis, reasoning that supervised features predictive of physical properties should also define the clustering geometry. K-means and PCA then operate on those same 96 representations and their alignment with alpha-v space is presented as support that the topology retains control-parameter information. Appendix E repeats the clustering with log-v-tuned parameters, but provides no representation fixed a priori, nested held-out clustering assessment, independent simulation ensemble, or external validation. The result is a useful parameter-aware atlas, not clean evidence that topology discovered the states without labels.

key_findings.claim: Time-resolved diagrams suggest a smooth-to-discontinuous change in domain formation near alpha approximately 2, but the quantitative transition statistic is empirically designed and does not establish a phase boundary.
key_findings.evidence: The paper contrasts two final labyrinthine states whose histograms, Fourier spectra, images, and persistence diagrams evolve differently. It defines intermediate-state birth, death, and lifetime masks from histogram peaks and standard deviations, then reports normalized maximum generation and growth ratios that fall toward zero around alpha 1.7 to 2 across sweep rates. The masks were chosen after empirical inspection, every curve is normalized to its alpha=1 value, no absolute counts or uncertainty bars appear, and only a small parameter grid is shown.

key_findings.claim: The reduced quartic energy gives a plausible local account of one-well versus metastable two-well dynamics, but it is a candidate explanation rather than a fitted or predictively validated reduction.
key_findings.evidence: Under an isomorphic-domain approximation, the full TDGL Hamiltonian is reduced to H(phi)=w0+w1 phi+w2 phi squared+w4 phi fourth with w4 positive, w1 changing sign during the field sweep, and w2 proportional to negative alpha plus an unknown constant. The cubic stationary-point discriminant has the correct qualitative sign interpretation when w4 is positive: positive means three stationary points and hence two local minima separated by a maximum, while negative means one. However, fixed domain area and boundary, constant exterior magnetization, isomorphic geometry, and unspecified C1 and C2 prevent derivation of the observed alpha approximately 2 threshold; no reduction parameters are fit and no held-out dynamics are predicted.

key_findings.claim: Classical summaries are not benchmarked even though the paper's own figures show that images, intensity histograms, and Fourier spectra visibly distinguish its showcase dynamics.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 8 places image, histogram, Fourier, and persistence representations side by side, and Section 6 acknowledges that Fourier peak structure can distinguish states I and V and that histograms directly expose intradomain fluctuations and continuous or discontinuous growth. The asserted advantage is that persistent homology unifies both kinds of information, but there is no comparison against pixels, Fourier descriptors, histograms, structure factors, Minkowski functionals, conventional morphology, or learned image embeddings in either regression or clustering.

key_findings.claim: The reported validation can interpolate a deterministic parameter surface without demonstrating generalization across initial conditions or material heterogeneity.
key_findings.evidence: All simulations use the same initial state. The Hamiltonian includes a random spatial anisotropy field lambda(r), yet the manuscript does not state that independent disorder realizations or seeds are drawn per sample. It also retains only 96 simulations whose numerical errors did not diverge, without reporting attempted count, excluded regions, or failure correlation with alpha and v. Thus nested cross-validation across snapshots need not test robustness to new initial states, new disorder fields, or solver failures.

key_findings.claim: The diagram and its displayed inverse locations are computed with nonidentical cubical conventions, so the visual localization is explicitly approximate.
key_findings.evidence: GUDHI computes the persistent homology using a pixel coverage that joins diagonal neighbors through pixel corners and boundaries. HomCloud, used to retrieve death-cube centers for Figures 5 and 9, places a zero-cube at each pixel center. Appendix C concedes that not all GUDHI rectangle locations are extracted and that HomCloud yields only approximate properties. This does not invalidate the persistence diagram, but it weakens pixel-level mechanistic interpretation of the highlighted death locations.

key_findings.claim: Several internal inconsistencies and omissions make exact replication difficult.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 and Section 2 specify alpha from 1 to 4, but the regression dataset is described as alpha from 1 to 5 and the next paragraph again calls its range 1 to 4. Figure 6(c)'s caption labels the horizontal axis as true alpha although the panel predicts log v. The manuscript does not report random seeds, the number of permutation repetitions, exact p-values, fold assignments, cluster initializations, attempted versus discarded simulations, or all selected vectorization hyperparameters in machine-readable form.

key_findings.claim: The study is simulation-closed and its code and data are not openly reproducible as of the audit date.
key_findings.evidence: Every result is generated by the authors' known TDGL simulator; no measured magnetic-domain sequence or independent simulator is evaluated. The arXiv v2 manuscript contains no code, repository, or data-release link. The Physica D version of record states only that data will be made available on request, and an exact-title GitHub repository search returned zero repositories on 2026-08-23. GUDHI and HomCloud are named libraries, but the simulation and analysis scripts, parameter draws, raw fields, and splits are absent.

method.core_idea: Use persistent homology as a common representation of global domain outline, local grayscale fluctuation, and their time evolution; supervise its vectorization with known simulator parameters; localize influential diagram regions back into images; cluster final snapshots; and use the resulting pattern groups to propose a low-dimensional energy mechanism.
method.mechanism: Simulate a periodic two-dimensional time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau magnetic field while varying anisotropy alpha and external-field sweep rate v; compute one-dimensional cubical persistence diagrams from superlevel sets of each grayscale field; rasterize diagrams with an unweighted Gaussian density; tune ridge and representation hyperparameters by nested cross-validation for alpha or log v; inspect long- and short-life diagram regions and approximate death cubes; run K-means and PCA on the selected final-snapshot representation; compare time-indexed diagrams for representative classes; define empirical intermediate-state masks; and reduce the Hamiltonian to a scalar quartic whose stationary-point discriminant distinguishes one- and two-minimum regimes.
assumptions: The two-dimensional TDGL model with fixed exchange, dipole, disorder, and field parameters captures the magnetic-domain mechanisms of interest.
A snapshot at twice the field-zero time represents a sufficiently stable and characteristic state.
One-dimensional superlevel-set persistence contains the relevant global and intradomain information; zero-dimensional and essential periodic classes are not required.
Near-diagonal generators are physical fluctuations rather than discretization or measurement noise, despite omitting lifetime weighting.
The manually selected long- and short-life regions have consistent physical meaning across alpha and v.
Nested sample-level cross-validation is a valid generalization test even when all simulations share an initial state and may share a disorder realization.
Nondivergent simulations are representative of the full requested parameter distribution.
Supervised alpha- or v-tuned persistence features can be reused for unsupervised clustering without materially biasing the discovered parameter geometry.
Euclidean K-means on a high-dimensional persistence image and the elbow-selected K=11 expose meaningful physical states in a sample of 96.
The GUDHI diagram and HomCloud death-cube approximation are close enough for pixel-level inverse interpretation.
Empirical histogram-derived diagram masks validly identify intermediate generation and growth states.
An isomorphic inverse domain with fixed area and boundary and constant exterior magnetization is an adequate scalar reduction near domain generation.
Unspecified proportionality constants in w1 and w2 do not alter the qualitative alpha dependence used to interpret the discriminant.
The analogy between low-alpha continuous formation and spinodal decomposition, and between high-alpha discontinuous formation and nucleation-growth, transfers beyond the simulator.

techniques.role: Generates 512 by 512 periodic magnetic-moment fields under anisotropy and field-sweep controls.
Encodes one-dimensional holes across grayscale thresholds with a cubical filtration.
Convolves birth-death points with Gaussian kernels and samples an M by M vector without lifetime weighting.
Separates manually delineated long- and short-life regions for physical interpretation and ablation-like regressions.
Uses nested cross-validation to tune regularization and persistence-image hyperparameters while estimating alpha or log v.
Uses HomCloud death cubes to approximately map selected persistence generators back to pixels.
Partitions supervised-selected persistent images into 11 clusters and visualizes them in alpha-v space.
Compresses the same features to two principal components for a low-dimensional parameter trajectory.
Compares persistence-diagram evolution across representative continuous and discontinuous formation trajectories.
Counts empirically defined intermediate-state generators during domain generation and growth.
Derives, but does not statistically fit, a scalar quartic energy and reasons from its stationary-point discriminant.

evaluations.setting: Ninety-six nondivergent final TDGL snapshots with alpha sampled uniformly and log10 v sampled from negative four to negative two.
evaluations.metric: Outer-fold RMSE and R-squared under nested cross-validated ridge regression.
evaluations.result: Full-diagram alpha RMSE is reported as about 0.001 with R-squared above 0.99; log-v prediction is substantially noisier.
evaluations.baseline: Long-only and short-only diagram regions; no raw-image, histogram, Fourier, morphology, nonlinear, or learned-feature baseline.

evaluations.setting: Regression of log10 sweep rate from all, long-life, and short-life persistent-image regions.
evaluations.metric: RMSE relative to a shuffled-label distribution.
evaluations.result: All three observed errors are described as significantly better than permutation, but repetitions, exact p-values, confidence intervals, and numeric RMSE table are absent.

evaluations.setting: Final-snapshot topology clustering on the same 96 persistent-image vectors selected by alpha regression.
evaluations.metric: Elbow criterion, qualitative parameter-space coherence, and two-component PCA variance.
evaluations.result: K=11 colors form smooth regions in alpha-v space and two PCs explain more than 85 percent of variance; six physical regions are then manually drawn.
evaluations.baseline: No representation fixed independently of labels and no held-out clustering metric.

evaluations.metric: Visual agreement of partitions in alpha-v space.
evaluations.result: Alpha-tuned and log-v-tuned vectorizations give the same K-means labels according to the text; hierarchical K=11 and polynomial spectral K=9 maps are broadly similar but not identical.
evaluations.baseline: Three clustering methods under selected hyperparameters, without stability distributions or external labels.

evaluations.setting: Inverse localization of representative long-, intermediate-, and short-life generators.
evaluations.metric: Visual placement of HomCloud death cubes over magnetic fields.
evaluations.result: Long generators align with isolated domain structure and short generators with local fluctuation peaks in the presented examples.
evaluations.baseline: Qualitative inspection only; the localization complex differs from the GUDHI complex that generated the diagram.

evaluations.setting: Time evolution of representative low-alpha state I and high-alpha state V, both labyrinthine at the final time.
evaluations.metric: Images, intensity histograms, Fourier spectra, persistence diagrams, and intermediate-generator ratios.
evaluations.result: Low alpha changes continuously while high alpha shows delayed, abrupt inverse-domain formation; normalized intermediate ratios decline near alpha about 2.
evaluations.baseline: Side-by-side descriptive curves without replicate uncertainty, predeclared thresholds, or independent phase labels.

evaluations.setting: Analytical reduction of the TDGL energy during inverse-domain generation.
evaluations.metric: Sign of the derivative cubic's discriminant.
evaluations.result: The proposed coefficients allow one minimum at lower alpha and metastable two-minimum structure at higher alpha, qualitatively matching continuous versus nucleation-like schematics.
evaluations.baseline: No fit to full-field energy, no reduced-dynamics rollout, and no held-out quantitative prediction.

evaluations.setting: Reproducibility audit of arXiv v2 and the December 2024 Physica D version of record as of 2026-08-23.
evaluations.metric: Availability of source, simulation code, analysis code, fields, parameter draws, splits, and seeds.
evaluations.result: The paper identifies GUDHI and HomCloud but releases none of its own implementation or data; the publisher states data are available on request and exact-title GitHub repository search returns no repository.
evaluations.baseline: Public libraries are available, but they are insufficient to reproduce the simulator-specific pipeline.

limitations: All scientific evidence is generated by a known simulator and no real magnetic-domain experiment or independent simulation code is analyzed.
Only 96 accepted simulations support high-dimensional vectorization, supervised tuning, 11-way clustering, PCA, and mechanism inference.
All simulations share one initial state, and independent quenched-disorder realizations or random seeds are not documented.
Runs with divergent numerical errors are excluded without attempted count or a missingness analysis over alpha-v space.
The alpha domain is internally inconsistent: 1 to 4 in Table 2, 1 to 5 in the regression-data description, then called 1 to 4 again.
Short-lived features are retained as signal without image-noise, pixel-resolution, filtration-convention, or perturbation robustness tests.
Persistent-homology stability does not by itself validate the full vectorization, supervised hyperparameter selection, region drawing, K selection, and clustering pipeline.
No non-TDA baseline tests whether topology improves prediction, discovery, or interpretability over statistics visibly present in the images, histograms, and Fourier spectra.
Supervised representation tuning and unsupervised state discovery reuse the same labels and same samples.
The 11 computed clusters and six manually drawn pattern states have no formal correspondence or independent physical ground truth.
The log-v result is assessed against a trivial permutation null rather than a competitive estimator, and its practical accuracy is not established.
HomCloud visual localization is only an approximation to the GUDHI cubical complex used to produce persistence diagrams.
The empirical intermediate-state masks, normalization, and alpha approximately 2 transition were not preregistered or validated on held-out trajectories.
The scalar energy reduction assumes isomorphic fixed geometry and leaves constants unspecified, so it cannot derive the claimed boundary or make quantitative predictions.
Simulation and analysis code, data, selected hyperparameters, seeds, folds, and cluster initializations are unavailable.
failure_modes: A fixed disorder field or shared initial state can let cross-validation interpolate a deterministic two-parameter surface while failing on new material realizations.
Supervised alpha tuning can manufacture a feature geometry whose subsequent clustering predictably aligns with alpha, creating circular discovery evidence.
K=11 on 96 points can yield unstable small clusters whose colors and manual consolidation change with initialization, scaling, or a few simulations.
Near-diagonal topological points can be dominated by pixel noise, numerical solver artifacts, or resolution changes while being interpreted as intradomain physics.
Changing diagonal connectivity, essential-cycle handling, filtration sign, or periodic-boundary conventions can move or remove generators and their physical interpretation.
Approximate HomCloud death locations can be attributed to the wrong local structure relative to the GUDHI diagram.
Divergent-run deletion can remove exactly the rapid-transition regime central to the claimed continuous-to-discontinuous change.
A normalized ratio can appear to vanish near alpha 2 even when absolute intermediate counts, total generator counts, or replicate variance tell a different story.
Fourier or histogram features may explain the same classification, making the claimed need for persistent homology an untested representation preference.
The quartic reduction can narrate two wells for many choices of unknown constants without reproducing the actual field trajectory, domain geometry, or transition threshold.
The method can rediscover simulator controls yet fail to reveal a mechanism in real data where parameters, initial states, noise, and model mismatch are unknown.
reusable_insights: Treat near-diagonal generators as a hypothesis to test rather than automatically discarding them; compare their predictive value under controlled noise and resolution perturbations.
Separate long- and short-life regions by physical inverse localization, but freeze region definitions before outcome evaluation and report sensitivity to boundaries.
Use topology as a bridge from global shape and local intensity distribution into one feature space, then benchmark against the union of the classical summaries it is meant to replace.

Cross-fit representation selection and clustering: learn persistence-image parameters on one simulation ensemble, freeze them, and assess cluster stability and physical coherence on independent initial states and disorder fields.
Track persistence generators through time with vineyard, zigzag, or multiparameter methods rather than comparing independently computed snapshots and empirical masks.
Validate inverse localization with intervention: perturb the proposed death-cube neighborhood and test the predicted diagram and physical changes.
Report simulator failure as an outcome surface rather than silently dropping divergent runs; numerical instability may identify scientifically important regimes.
Convert a visually motivated energy reduction into a falsifiable surrogate by fitting coefficients on training trajectories and predicting held-out switching times, barriers, and domain statistics.
Preserve direct links among a diagram region, source pixels, control parameters, and downstream physical quantities; this traceability is the strongest part of the proposed workflow.
Use experimental sequences or at least an independently implemented simulator to distinguish mechanism recovery from closed-loop rediscovery of a generative model.
open_questions: Do alpha and sweep-rate predictions survive new initial conditions and independently sampled spatial anisotropy fields?
How many simulations were attempted, which diverged, and does divergence concentrate near the proposed mechanism boundary?

Does persistent homology outperform raw pixels, histograms plus Fourier features, structure factors, Minkowski functionals, morphology descriptors, or a small convolutional encoder under matched nested cross-validation?
Are the 11 clusters stable across simulation seeds, persistence grids, image resolutions, noise levels, diagram distances, and K-selection criteria?
Can a feature representation selected without alpha or v labels recover the same cluster geometry on a held-out ensemble?
What is the adjusted-Rand or transport agreement between K-means, hierarchical, spectral, direct-diagram K-means, and manual six-state labels?
Are short-lived generators stable under realistic magnetic-imaging noise and pixel resampling, or are they primarily numerical texture?
How are essential one-cycles on the periodic lattice handled, and do alternative cubical diagonal-connectivity conventions change results?
Can exact GUDHI generators be localized instead of using a different HomCloud complex, and do interventions at those pixels support the proposed causal interpretation?
Can temporally linked persistence track individual domain births, merges, and deaths more faithfully than independently thresholding each snapshot?
Can the quartic coefficients and constants be estimated from the full Hamiltonian and then predict the alpha transition, switching delay, and metastable lifetime out of sample?
Does the proposed spinodal-versus-nucleation interpretation agree with independently measured structure-factor growth rates, critical nuclei, barrier crossing, and experimental magnetic movies?
Would uncertainty-aware hierarchical modeling distinguish within-parameter stochastic variability from between-parameter topology?
Can the full code, parameter draws, raw fields, folds, seeds, and failed runs be released so the unusually small alpha RMSE can be independently reproduced?

competitive_landscape.title: Topological Microstructure Analysis Using Persistence Landscapes
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest foundational predecessor for recovering phase-field parameters and stage from persistent summaries of evolving microstructures.
competitive_landscape.difference: Dlotko and Wanner study Cahn-Hilliard phase separation with averaged persistence landscapes and explicitly motivate robustness to noise and experimental-to-simulation comparison. The present paper adds grayscale inverse localization, supervised persistence-image regions, clustering, and a magnetic reduced-energy narrative, but does not perform comparable noise analysis or experimental validation.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v1; related Physica D 2016 article

competitive_landscape.title: Persistence Images: A Stable Vector Representation of Persistent Homology
competitive_landscape.relationship: Methodological antecedent for the Gaussian-grid vectorization and physical-parameter inference used here.
competitive_landscape.difference: Adams et al. define persistence images, prove representation stability under stated weighting conditions, compare discriminatory power with other summaries, and infer parameters of dynamical systems. This paper removes lifetime weighting to retain short-lived points, so the relevance of that stability theory to its chosen representation and downstream clusters must be re-established empirically.

competitive_landscape.title: Persistence Diagrams with Linear Machine Learning Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct methodological predecessor for interpretable linear weights and inverse analysis from persistence images back to original structures.
competitive_landscape.difference: Obayashi and Hiraoka establish the general persistence-image plus linear-model inverse-analysis framework for point clouds and cubical sets. The present work applies that framework to magnetic patterns and extends it into time evolution and energy interpretation; the generic inverse-analysis mechanism itself is prior work.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretable Phase Detection and Classification with Persistent Homology
competitive_landscape.relationship: Competing interpretable phase-discovery pipeline using persistence images and simple supervised models on statistical-physics systems.
competitive_landscape.difference: Cole, Loges, and Shiu recover recognizable order parameters from logistic-regression weights and locate known lattice-spin transitions. The magnetic-pattern paper targets process mechanisms and grayscale domains, but its alpha-informed representation and manually drawn states provide weaker independence between supervision and discovery.

competitive_landscape.title: Persistent homology classifies parameter dependence of patterns in Turing systems
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest later application of topological clustering to parameter-dependent self-organizing reaction-diffusion patterns.
competitive_landscape.difference: Spector, Harrington, and Gaffney cluster topological summaries across Turing parameter spaces and discuss using clusters to refine priors for detailed parameter estimation. It offers a direct post-publication comparator for whether the magnetic workflow's states recur across models, but likewise requires care in separating parameter-aware maps from independent mechanism validation.

competitive_landscape.title: k-Means Clustering for Persistent Homology
competitive_landscape.relationship: Competing clustering formulation directly on persistence diagrams or measures.
competitive_landscape.difference: Cao, Leung, and Monod prove convergence properties and report that direct diagram or persistence-measure K-means can outperform vectorized representations. That creates an untested alternative to Euclidean K-means on an alpha-tuned Gaussian grid and could remove sensitivity to M and sigma while providing a more topology-native geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Quasi Zigzag Persistence: A Topological Framework for Analyzing Time-Varying Data
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current topology-native alternative for coupling structure across time rather than treating magnetic snapshots independently.
competitive_landscape.difference: Dey and Samaga combine multiparameter and zigzag persistence into a stable invariant that captures static and dynamic features at multiple scales. Applying such temporal correspondence to domain births, merges, and deaths could replace this paper's empirically drawn intermediate-state masks, though QZPH has not yet been validated on magnetic patterns.

competitive_landscape.title: Continuation of Point Clouds via Persistence Diagrams
competitive_landscape.relationship: Alternative inverse-topology method that actively constructs source-space changes realizing target diagram changes.
competitive_landscape.difference: Gameiro, Hiraoka, and Obayashi differentiate the persistence map and use continuation to move a point cloud toward a target diagram. The magnetic paper only visualizes approximate death cubes and correlates them with physical structures; intervention or continuation could turn that descriptive inverse map into a stronger causal test.

competitive_landscape.title: Topology and control of self-assembled domain patterns in low-dimensional ferroelectrics
competitive_landscape.relationship: Physics-side comparator that distinguishes spinodal decomposition and nucleation in domain evolution using simulations, structure factors, energy barriers, and experiments.
competitive_landscape.difference: Nahas et al. validate domain pathways with growth rates, critical nucleus size, interaction-energy arguments, molecular-dynamics sequences, and experimental PFM images. The paper under review reaches a similar spinodal-versus-nucleation narrative from TDGL topology but lacks independent experimental evidence, quantitative barrier estimation, or structure-factor validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Persistent Homology Analysis for Materials Research and Persistent Homology Software: HomCloud
competitive_landscape.relationship: Software and materials-analysis foundation for the paper's generator localization and interpretability claims.
competitive_landscape.difference: Obayashi, Nakamura, and Hiraoka document HomCloud and broader materials use cases. The magnetic paper combines HomCloud localization with GUDHI diagrams computed under another cubical convention, creating an implementation-specific approximation that a single consistent library or exact-cycle extraction should test.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A general TDA and machine-learning procedure can classify nontrivial magnetic-domain states, map their geometric signatures to physical formation dynamics, and motivate a reduced model revealing the mechanism.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper combines final-state parameter regression, inverse localization of long- and short-life diagram regions, an 11-cluster parameter atlas, time-evolving persistence diagrams, empirical intermediate-state counts, and a quartic energy reduction in one worked TDGL system.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The most credible novelty is the end-to-end assembly of established persistent-image regression and inverse analysis into a physically narrated magnetic-domain workflow, especially treating near-diagonal grayscale features as candidate signal. Parameter recovery, persistence-image interpretability, topological phase classification, and microstructure inference all have clear predecessors. The mechanism claim remains exploratory because supervised feature tuning leaks known controls into the cluster map, classical baselines and independent seeds are absent, death localization is approximate, and the reduced model is not fit or tested. A stronger successor would freeze the representation before clustering, validate across independent disorder and experimental movies, compare topology to classical morphology, track generators through time, and require the reduced energy to make held-out predictions.

reviewer_notes: Read all 54 pages of arXiv v2, including the derivations and Appendices A-G; inspected the parameter table, all main result figures, regression scatter and bar plots, cluster/PCA maps, time-evolution grids, generator overlays, transition-ratio curves, robustness appendices, and quartic-energy derivation at original rendered resolution. The discriminant sign was independently checked for dH/dphi=4w4 phi cubed+2w2 phi+w1 with w4 positive. Primary-source competitor records and the December 2024 Physica D version were checked on 2026-08-23. The publisher reports data only on request; no paper-specific code link appears in the manuscript or arXiv record, and exact-title GitHub repository search returned zero projects. Minor exposition issue: page 3 says a Betti number constitutes the Euler characteristic, whereas Euler characteristic is the alternating sum across Betti numbers. The most material audit finding is supervised representation selection before ostensibly unsupervised clustering, not that exposition error.
